Empirical Research Plan: The Long-Run Growth Effects of Tropical Cyclones  

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy Dynamic difference-in-differences / event-study (a distributed-lag “impulse-response” design).

Why appropriate  
•  Exogenous, sharp, and plausibly random within-country year-to-year variation in cyclone intensity supplies repeated “shocks.”  
•  Panel (1950-2008, 180+ countries) lets us difference out time-invariant country factors with country fixed effects and global shocks with year fixed effects.  
•  Leads and lags of the shock trace out the growth path up to ±15 years, allowing us to discriminate among “creative destruction,” “build-back-better,” “full recovery,” and “no recovery.”  
•  Treatment intensity is continuous (wind speed / energy); the model therefore estimates semi-elasticities of growth with respect to physical cyclone energy without dichotomising information.

Mathematically (baseline specification)

Δln GDPpc_{c,t+h} = Σ_{k=0}^K β_k Shock_{c,t–k} + γ_c + δ_t + X_{c,t} θ + ε_{c,t+h}

where Shock_{c,t} is the contemporaneous cyclone energy (or indicator for a “severe” cyclone), γ_c are country FE, δ_t year FE, and h indexes horizons.  

Local projections (Jordà 2005) will be used to obtain IRFs at each horizon h; coefficients β_0 … β_K form the event-study pattern.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
A. Continuous: Power Dissipation Density (PDD) aggregated to country-year (10^{13} Watts).  
B. Binary (used for event timing): SevereCyclone_{c,t}=1 if max wind speed ≥ 33 m s⁻¹ (≥64 kt, Saffir-Simpson Cat 1).

Control group  
The same country in years without a severe cyclone (or with low PDD). Untreated observations therefore supply the counterfactual growth path.

Treatment timing / event date  
Year t when SevereCyclone_{c,t}=1; event time τ = year – t. Leads (τ<0) test for pre-trends; lags (τ≥0) estimate persistence.

(An RDD is not used; no geographic running variable is required because we exploit time variation within country.)

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Quasi-random timing/intensity of cyclones conditional on country FE and common year shocks (parallel-trends in levels of GDP absent the storm).  
Plausibility: Meteorological processes are orthogonal to national macroeconomic conditions; credible.

A2. No anticipation / investment surge just before the hit.  
Plausibility: Storm formation is only predictable a few days ahead, far shorter than horizon of annual macro data.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no cross-country spillovers).  
Plausibility: Some spillovers through trade and aid are possible but likely second-order; will include global year FE and bilateral trade controls in robustness.

A4. Shocks are exogenous to measurement error in GDP (GDP mis-measurement not correlated with cyclone incidence).  
Plausibility reasonable; Penn World Tables revisions are unrelated to storm years.

A5. Correct dynamic specification and serial-correlation-robust inference.  
Addressed via local projections and Driscoll–Kraay / cluster by country SEs.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Omitted global climate phenomena (e.g. ENSO) that influence both cyclone activity and growth.  
Mitigation: Control for annual Niño3.4 index, global commodity prices, temperature & precipitation; include region×year fixed effects.

T2. Measurement error in cyclone exposure (wind-field modelling error).  
Mitigation: Use both PDD and max-wind measures; instrument reported damage (EM-DAT) with PDD as a robustness check; average over 3-year windows to reduce noise.

T3. Serial correlation / multiple shocks.  
Mitigation:  a) Cluster SEs at country level; b) saturation of lags and cumulative effect calculation; c) collapse multiple hits within a five-year window to a single event in robustness.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# --- 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE regressions
library(sandwich)     # robust vcov
library(lmtest)       # coeftest
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
gdp   <- fread("pwt_gdp_pc.csv")          # columns: iso, year, gdp_pc
storm <- fread("cyclone_exposure.csv")    # iso, year, max_wind, pdd
clim  <- fread("climate_controls.csv")    # iso, year, temp, precip, nino34

# --- 2. Merge & construct variables ------------------------------------------
dat <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, by=c("iso","year"), all=TRUE),
              list(gdp, storm, clim))

# Log levels and growth
dat[, ln_gdppc := log(gdp_pc)]
setorder(dat, iso, year)
dat[, g_gdppc := ln_gdppc - shift(ln_gdppc), by = iso]    # Δln GDP per cap

# Treatment variables
threshold <- 33    # m/s (Cat 1)
dat[, severe := as.integer(max_wind >= threshold)]
dat[, pdd_norm := (pdd)/1e13]              # scale

# Lags/leads for event-study (±10 yrs)
for(L in -5:10){
  dat[, paste0("sev_leadlag_", L) :=
        shift(severe, n = -L, type = "lag"), by = iso]
}

# --- 3. Baseline local projection (h=0,…,10) ---------------------------------
results <- list()
H <- 10
for(h in 0:H){
  dat[, g_future := shift(ln_gdppc, -h) - ln_gdppc, by=iso]  # Δh ln GDP
  fml <- as.formula(paste0(
          "g_future ~ pdd_norm + temp + precip + nino34 | iso + year"))
  results[[h+1]] <- feols(fml, data = dat, cluster = "iso")
}

# collect IRF
irf <- data.table(h = 0:H,
                  beta = sapply(results, coef)[ "pdd_norm", ],
                  se = sapply(results,
                          function(m) sqrt(diag(vcov_cluster(m))[ "pdd_norm" ])))
irf[, `:=`(lower = beta - 1.96*se, upper = beta + 1.96*se)]

# Plot
ggplot(irf, aes(h, beta))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower, ymax=upper), alpha=.2)+
  geom_line()+geom_point()+
  labs(y="Semi-elasticity Δh ln GDP per capita / PDD", x="Years after cyclone")

# --- 4. Robustness: placebo leads (-5 to -1) ---------------------------------
placebo_fml <- as.formula(
  paste0("g_gdppc ~ ", paste(paste0("sev_leadlag_", -5:-1), collapse = " + "),
         " + temp + precip + nino34 | iso + year"))
placebo_mod <- feols(placebo_fml, data = dat, cluster = "iso")
etable(placebo_mod, drop = "temp|precip|nino")  # expect no significant coeffs
```

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------
Direction: Negative on impact (β₀<0).  
Magnitude (ball-park): A one-standard-deviation rise in PDD (≈ 3×10^{12} W) is expected to lower contemporaneous GDP per capita growth by about 0.5–1 percentage points, with partial but not full rebound; cumulative 10-year loss ≈ 3–5 percent of counterfactual output in highly exposed countries. I expect no long-run “build-back-better” overshoot.

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)

C1: Exogeneity of treatment timing/intensity…….……1  
C2: Parallel pre-trends (validated by placebo leads)…1  
C3: No spillovers/interference……………………………0.5  
C4: Stable sample / no selective attrition………………1  
C5: Correct SEs & dynamic specification………………1  

Overall: 4.5 / 5 – design is credibly causal with minor residual concern about cross-country spillovers through trade and aid.
